equation_request.abstract: We investigate the subclass of reversible functions that are self-inverse and relate them to reversible circuits that are equal to their reverse circuit, which are called palindromic circuits. We precisely determine which self-inverse functions can be realized as a palindromic circuit. For those functions that cannot be realized as a palidromic circuit, we find alternative palindromic representations that require an extra circuit line or quantum gates in their construction. Our analyses make use of involutions in the symmetric group $S_{2^{n}}$ which are isomorphic to self-inverse reversible function on $n$ variables.

specification.problem: Characterize which self-inverse reversible functions (involutions in S_{2^n}) can be realized as palindromic reversible circuits (circuits equal to their reverse), and construct alternatives with an extra line or quantum gates when not possible. The abstract gives no precise characterization criterion.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Background definitions only, plus a tiny assumed instance: n=2 bits, circuits over a gate library of self-inverse gates (e.g. NOT/CNOT/Toffoli). Covers the relation between palindromic circuits and involutions. The actual characterization theorem, the extra-line construction, and the quantum-gate construction are outside scope.

symbols.meaning: reversible function on n bits, as a permutation of {0,...,2^n-1}
reversible circuit as a cascade of gates

equations.label: Self-inverse function
equations.description: Self-inverse reversible functions are involutions in the symmetric group on 2^n points (identity included).
equations.abstract_quote: involutions in the symmetric group $S_{2^{n}}$ which are isomorphic to self-inverse reversible function on $n$ variables
equations.justification: The abstract states the isomorphism between involutions and self-inverse functions; the defining relation f^2=id is the standard meaning of involution.
assumptions: Identity is counted as an involution

equations.label: Palindromic circuit
equations.description: A circuit is palindromic if it equals its reverse, i.e. the gate sequence reads the same in both directions.
equations.abstract_quote: reversible circuits that are equal to their reverse circuit, which are called palindromic circuits
equations.justification: Direct reading of the definition as gate-sequence equality.
assumptions: Equality is of gate sequences, not just of realized functions

equations.label: Reverse circuit realizes inverse
equations.description: With self-inverse gates, the reverse circuit computes the inverse function.
equations.justification: Standard: (g_k\cdots g_1) is the inverse of g_1\cdots g_k when each gate is an involution.

equations.label: Palindromic implies self-inverse
equations.description: Any palindromic circuit over self-inverse gates realizes an involution; the converse (which involutions have a palindromic realization) is the paper's question and is not reconstructed.
equations.abstract_quote: We precisely determine which self-inverse functions can be realized as a palindromic circuit.
equations.justification: Follows from eq_2 and eq_3; the converse criterion is not given in the abstract.

registers.name: x
registers.role: data lines carrying the bit string, integer encoding x=\sum x_i 2^i (assumed)

registers.name: anc
registers.role: extra line used in the alternative palindromic representation (construction not specified)

steps.description: Represent a self-inverse reversible function on n bits as an involution in S_{2^n}.
Synthesize a circuit over self-inverse gates and test whether its gate sequence is palindromic.
Note that palindromic realizations necessarily give involutions; the exact criterion for which involutions admit them is needed but not given.

assumptions: Tiny instance n=2 chosen as the smallest useful illustration
Gate library consists of self-inverse gates
missing_information: Exact criterion for which involutions admit palindromic circuits
Gate library used in the paper
